author: Emily Ross
title: Hegseth's Plane Makes Emergency Landing in UK
text:
A military plane carrying War Secretary Pete Hegseth made an emergency landing in the United Kingdom on Wednesday afternoon, officials confirmed.
The Air Force C-32 aircraft was returning from a NATO Defense Ministers meeting in Brussels when the incident occurred.
Emergency Declared Mid-Flight
Flight-tracking data showed the aircraft rapidly descending and turning back toward the U.K. shortly before 2 p.m. Eastern Time.
“The Air Force C-32 carrying Secretary Pete Hegseth has declared an emergency over the Atlantic,” journalist Nick Sortor posted on X.
He said the plane had dropped to 10,000 feet and reversed course mid-flight.
“Plane is squawking 7700, which could mean an engine failure, medical issue, onboard fire, or another general emergency,” Sortor added.
Chief Pentagon Spokesman Sean Parnell confirmed the emergency landing minutes later.
“On the way back to the United States from NATO’s Defense Ministers meeting, Secretary of War Hegseth’s plane made an unscheduled landing in the United Kingdom,” Parnell said.
He explained the diversion was due to a crack in the aircraft’s windshield.
Parnell said the landing followed standard emergency procedures and that everyone onboard was safe.
Hegseth Responds
Hegseth confirmed his safety in a brief post on X.
“All good. Thank God. Continue mission!” he wrote.
The Secretary’s message quickly went viral among supporters relieved by the update.
Hegseth had been returning from the NATO Ministers of Defense Meeting in Brussels, Belgium.
The session was chaired by NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte and focused on defense strategy and alliance priorities.
Rutte praised U.S. leadership and reaffirmed NATO unity in the face of global threats.
Mission Continues
The Pentagon said a replacement aircraft would be dispatched to return Hegseth and his delegation to Washington.
Officials emphasized that operations and communications were not disrupted by the incident.
Hegseth is expected to resume his schedule once back in the United States.
By Wednesday evening, Pentagon officials confirmed the investigation into the windshield damage was underway.
No injuries or mechanical fires were reported aboard the aircraft.
The emergency landing was described as “precautionary and successful.”
Hegseth’s quick response and calm demeanor drew praise from colleagues and military leaders.
By nightfall, the Secretary was back in contact with NATO counterparts, reaffirming that “the mission continues.”
